facts.fact: a squeezing, wrenching, grasping, covetous old sinner, hard as flint
facts.quote: a squeezing, wrenching, grasping, scraping, clutching, covetous, old sinner

facts.fact: cold features: pointed nose nipped red, thin blue lips, a stiff frosty gait
facts.quote: The cold within him froze his old features, nipped his pointed nose, shrivelled his cheek, stiffened his gait

facts.fact: hard, secret, self-contained, and solitary, striking no generous fire from anyone
facts.quote: Hard and sharp as flint, from which no steel had ever struck out generous fire; secret, and self-contained, and solitary as an oyster.

facts.fact: openly scorns Christmas cheer and calls the poor undeserving of merriment
facts.quote: What right have you to be merry? What reason have you to be merry? You're poor enough.

facts.fact: dismisses everything with his catchphrase 'Bah! Humbug!'
facts.quote: Bah!" said Scrooge, "Humbug!

facts.fact: former business partner of the late Jacob Marley; the firm is still called Scrooge and Marley
facts.quote: Scrooge and Marley. The firm was known as Scrooge and Marley.

facts.fact: refuses to donate to a charity collection, invoking prisons and workhouses instead
facts.quote: Are there no prisons?" asked Scrooge.

facts.fact: coldly rebuffs his nephew Fred's cheerful Christmas dinner invitation
facts.quote: Nephew!" returned the uncle sternly, "keep Christmas in your own way, and let me keep it in mine.

facts.fact: as a boy he was left alone at boarding school over Christmas until his sister Fan came to bring him home
facts.quote: You are quite a woman, little Fan!" exclaimed the boy.

facts.fact: was once engaged to a woman named Belle, who broke it off because his growing love of money had replaced his love for her
facts.quote: Another idol has displaced me

facts.fact: as a young man he was apprenticed to the jovial old Fezziwig, who threw joyous Christmas parties
facts.quote: Was I apprenticed here!

facts.fact: after his ghostly transformation, buys the prize turkey and has it sent anonymously to Bob Cratchit
facts.quote: I'll send it to Bob Cratchit's!

facts.fact: pretends to scold Bob for arriving late the next morning, then announces he is raising his salary
facts.quote: I am about to raise your salary!

facts.fact: becomes a second father to Tiny Tim, who does not die after all
facts.quote: to Tiny Tim, who did NOT die, he was a second father.

facts.fact: is transformed into as good a man as the old city knew, laughing heartily where he once growled
facts.quote: He became as good a friend, as good a master, and as good a man, as the good old city knew

facts.fact: curtly repeats 'Good afternoon!' to dismiss unwelcome conversation before his transformation
facts.quote: Good afternoon!" said Scrooge.

facts.fact: carries his own low temperature everywhere, even icing his office in hot weather
facts.quote: he iced his office in the dog-days; and didn't thaw it one degree at Christmas.

antiFacts.claim: generous and warm from the very beginning
antiFacts.why: he starts the story miserly and cold, only becoming generous after the ghostly visitations
he is repeatedly described as old (old sinner, old features)
his engagement to Belle was broken off, and the text never depicts him marrying anyone

antiFacts.claim: kind and generous to his clerk from the start
antiFacts.why: at the start he keeps the coal-box locked from Bob and grudges him a paid Christmas Day off
he has a nephew, Fred, who repeatedly invites him to dinner

facts.fact: Scrooge's underpaid clerk, earning only fifteen shillings a week for a wife and family
facts.quote: my clerk, with fifteen shillings a week, and a wife and family

facts.fact: father of a large family including Tiny Tim, a frail boy who needs a crutch and a leg iron
facts.quote: Tiny Tim upon his shoulder. Alas for Tiny Tim, he bore a little crutch, and had his limbs supported by an iron frame!

facts.fact: poor and threadbare, with a long comforter scarf since he has no greatcoat
facts.quote: the long ends of his white comforter dangling below his waist (for he boasted no great-coat)

facts.fact: slides on the ice down Cornhill with a line of boys and rushes home to play blindman's buff on Christmas Eve
facts.quote: went down a slide on Cornhill, at the end of a lane of boys, twenty times

facts.fact: a devoted father who holds Tiny Tim close and dreads losing him
facts.quote: Bob held his withered little hand in his, as if he loved the child, and wished to keep him by his side

facts.fact: toasts Scrooge as 'the Founder of the Feast' at Christmas dinner despite his wife's anger at their employer
facts.quote: I'll give you Mr. Scrooge, the Founder of the Feast!

facts.fact: remains cheerful and speaks pleasantly to his family despite poverty and hardship
facts.quote: Bob was very cheerful with them, and spoke pleasantly to all the family.

facts.fact: gently calls his wife 'my dear' and checks her sharp words for the children's sake
facts.quote: My dear," said Bob, "the children! Christmas Day.

facts.fact: arrives eighteen minutes late to work the day after Christmas and meekly apologizes to Scrooge
facts.quote: I am very sorry, sir," said Bob. "I am behind my time.

facts.fact: receives a raise and Scrooge's promise of help for his family after Scrooge's transformation
facts.quote: I'll raise your salary, and endeavour to assist your struggling family

facts.fact: works in 'the Tank,' a small cold cell-like office next to Scrooge's, with a fire so small it looks like a single coal
facts.quote: the clerk's fire was so very much smaller that it looked like one coal

facts.fact: is deeply touched when he recounts Scrooge's nephew Fred's unexpected kindness to him on the street
facts.quote: Bob told them of the extraordinary kindness of Mr. Scrooge's nephew

facts.fact: a proud family man who praises the Christmas goose and pudding as though they were unmatched delicacies
facts.quote: There never was such a goose. Bob said he didn't believe there ever was such a goose cooked.

facts.fact: mixes a hot drink of gin and lemons in a jug for the family to share at Christmas dinner
facts.quote: compounded some hot mixture in a jug with gin and lemons, and stirred it round and round and put it on the hob to simmer

facts.fact: in a vision of a possible future, grieves quietly and composes himself after Tiny Tim's death
facts.quote: Poor Bob sat down in it, and when he had thought a little and composed himself, he kissed the little face.

facts.fact: hopes to find his son Peter a situation that would earn five-and-sixpence a week
facts.quote: he had a situation in his eye for Master Peter, which would bring in, if obtained, full five-and-sixpence weekly

antiFacts.why: he earns only fifteen shillings a week and cannot even afford a greatcoat
he toasts Scrooge as 'the Founder of the Feast' and defends him when his wife grows angry
he has a large family including Tiny Tim, Peter, Belinda, Martha, and two younger children
he is Scrooge's clerk and employee; Jacob Marley was the business partner

antiFacts.claim: lives in a large, well-heated house
antiFacts.why: the Ghost blesses his modest four-roomed house, and his office fire at work is famously tiny
